sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Nalin Arora Hon'ble Vivek Chaudhary,J.
Hon'ble Om Prakash Shukla,J.
1.Sri Nalin Arora, Advocate has filed his vakalatnama on behalf of the opposite party no.3 today in the Court, which is taken on record.
2. Heard Shri A.Z. Siddiqui, learned Counsel for the petitioners, Shri Nalin Arora, learned Counsel for the opposite party No.3 and learned A.G.A. for the State-opposite parties.
3.The instant writ petition has been filed seeking following main relief:-

"a. Issue a writ in the nature of Certiorari or any other writ or order or direction quashing the impugned First Information Report No.255/2024 dated 24.11.2024 Bhupendra Jeet Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ... on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124410999/
1 lodged by the respondent no.3 under Section 316(2), 318(4), 352, 351(2) B.N.S. (Old Sections 406, 420, 504, 506 IPC) at Police Station Talkatora, District Lucknow against the petitioners, as contained in Annexure No.1 to the writ petition."
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is a civil dispute between the parties and the opposite party No.3 has tried to give colour to a civil dispute into criminal prosecution.
5. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.3 as well as learned A.G.A. for the State categorically denied the aforesaid contention of learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that amount of Rs.12,64,000/- of entire amount was received through cheque and the said amount was taken by the petitioner by playing fraud upon the opposite party no.3 claiming that the said property will be sold to the opposite party no.3, which is now bluntly refused.

entities.text: Bhupendra Jeet Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They further submit that the petitioners only wanted to deceive the opposite party No.3 and the entire proposal to sell the property in dispute was concocted and fabricated.

6. Having heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the material placed on record, this Court does not find any ground to interefere in the present petition as prima facie from the reading of the FIR cognizable offence is made out against the petitioner.
7.
In view of the above, the instant writ petition stands dismissed.
(Om Prakash Shukla, J) (Vivek Chaudhary, J) Order Date :- 12.12.2024 DiVYa  Bhupendra Jeet Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ...
